title: Noor and the Typewriter
premise: In 1938 in the fictional Baltic port city of Vellengard, Odile Voss, an apprentice clockmaker hiding a forged identity, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock. There she meets Noor Haddad, a census taker whose portable typewriter records more than names—it feeds a state registry deciding who will be granted passage on the last ship out before the borders close. As their wary alliance deepens into love, Odile must choose whether to trust Noor with the truth of her family's false papers, and when the registry is compromised, the two of them must decide which single remaining berth goes to Odile's ailing mother or her young brother. In the end, Odile alters the master clock to stall the registry's final transmission, buying Noor time to forge a second berth—though the escape costs Odile her anonymity, her city, and nearly Noor himself, who stays behind as the ship pulls away with a promise folded into a typed page.
about_author: Ivo Delacroix is the pen name of a former restorer of antique office machines who spent a decade repairing typewriters in archive basements across Northern Europe. Their fiction is drawn from family letters discovered sewn into the lining of a census ledger.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She is summoned from her uncle's clock shop to the observatory, where the master clock governing the city's official time has failed. Establishes her habit of invisibility and her forged family papers. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competent hands.

chapters.title: A Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Census taker Noor Haddad arrives at the Voss household with a portable typewriter, asking questions that drift from routine into dangerous territory about Odile's late father. Emotional beat: the first crack in the family's careful anonymity.

chapters.title: The Clock That Keeps the City
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Working alone at night in the observatory, Odile discovers the master clock has been deliberately tampered with—someone wants official time to drift. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into alarm.

chapters.title: Carbon and Confession
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor types up the day's census forms and notices an anomaly: the Voss entry has been flagged by a superior. He begins to suspect his work feeds something darker than statistics. Emotional beat: conscience stirring.

chapters.title: Berth One of Twelve
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The family learns the harbor office has posted the emigration list: twelve berths, one ship, and the registry's recommendations decide priority. Odile's mother is ill; her brother Tomas is fourteen. Emotional beat: hope curdling into arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Registry Room
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor delivers his ledgers to the Ministry and glimpses the ranking system—typewritten lists where a single keystroke moves a family from passage to refusal. He recognizes the Voss name near the bottom. Emotional beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: Overtime at Midnight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile catches a stranger tampering with the master clock again and, hiding, realizes the drift is designed to misdate official stamps—invalidating documents, including emigration papers. Emotional beat: the machinery of the state revealed as a weapon.

chapters.title: What the Typewriter Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor finds erased carbon ribbons in the office wastebasket and reconstructs deleted names—people struck from eligibility. He pockets one ribbon bearing the name Voss. Emotional beat: complicity turning to quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: Tea, Two Cups, No Lies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Odile and Noor, each probing the other, end up confessing in fragments—her forged papers, his flagged report. An uneasy alliance forms: he can amend the registry, she can prove the clock fraud. Emotional beat: trust offered like a held breath.

chapters.title: Mother's Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's mother, lucid for an evening, gives Odile her real name and the story behind the forgery, asking only that the family stay together. Emotional beat: love as inheritance and burden.

chapters.title: The Ministry's Clockmaker
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor is ordered to expedite the registry before the ship's departure and notices the deadline is keyed to the observatory's official time. The tampered clock is not a side effect—it is the mechanism. Emotional beat: horror of elegant design.

chapters.title: A Ribbons Worth of Names
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor copies the struck names and passes them to Odile through a repair ticket for his typewriter. Among them are families who will be refused passage without ever knowing why. Emotional beat: the weight of witness.

chapters.title: Tomas Counts the Days
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Young Tomas, sensing the stakes, offers to give up his berth to his mother; Odile refuses and lies to him about the odds. Emotional beat: protective love shading into its first cruelty.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns the Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Director Kelweg, the ministry official behind the clock tampering, summons both Odile and Noor, probing what they know. He offers Noor a promotion contingent on finalizing the Voss file. Emotional beat: power smiling with an open hand.

chapters.title: Eleven Berths
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A rival family's papers are invalidated by a mistimed stamp; their berth reopens. The family's chances shift, but so does the danger—Kelweg suspects insider interference. Emotional beat: hope that feels stolen.

chapters.title: The Choice, Drafted
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor can amend the registry for exactly one name without detection. He and Odile argue through the night—mother or brother—until Odile's mother settles it herself, typing her decision on Noor's machine: Tomas. Emotional beat: sacrifice made in ink.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Tower
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. To buy time for the amendment, Odile alters the master clock to hold official time frozen, stalling the registry's final transmission. Kelweg's men begin searching the observatory. Emotional beat: the invisible woman making herself the loudest thing in the city.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor is detained and questioned; Kelweg dangles the Voss file and Noor's career, then his freedom. Noor gives up nothing but a typed confession to a crime he didn't commit, buying Odile another hour. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty losing.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The amended registry slips through in the frozen minutes. Odile gets Tomas and her mother to the ship, but there is no berth—and no time—for herself. Emotional beat: the choice she made without letting anyone choose for her.

chapters.title: One Page, Folded Twice
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. As the ship sounds its horn, Noor escapes custody and reaches the pier too late to board, pressing a typed page into Odile's hand through the railing—coordinates, a name, a promise. Emotional beat: parting as an act of faith.

chapters.title: What the Clock Struck Last
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At sea, Odile reads the page and learns Kelweg has fallen, his fraud exposed by the frozen clock itself—her sabotage became the evidence. She winds her father's pocket watch and lets it run true for the first time. Emotional beat: grief and release in the same breath.

chapters.title: Noor and the Typewriter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. Two years later, in a new city, Odile repairs machines in a small shop. A customer enters carrying a familiar portable typewriter, ribbon worn thin. Noor sits down and begins to type. Emotional beat: reunion as a new first sentence.
